buildings.name: Advanced Replicators
buildings.description: Second-generation food synthesizers with a far larger pattern library, and meals people actually enjoy. Raises the system's food output by a percentage.

buildings.name: Basic Replicators
buildings.description: Industrial food synthesizers that turn raw organic stock into nourishing, if unexciting, meals. Raises the system's food output by a percentage.

buildings.name: Bunker Network
buildings.description: Fortified tunnels, weapons caches and trained militia that make every invasion a long, bloody slog. Strengthens ground defense.

buildings.name: Charge Collectors
buildings.description: Lightning rods the size of mountains, tapping the static that builds in the frozen air of arctic worlds. Raises the system's energy output.

buildings.name: Communications Grid
buildings.description: Dedicated subspace relays that keep a distant world in constant contact with its government. Fewer misunderstandings, fewer grievances.

buildings.name: Orbital Battery
buildings.description: Armed satellites ringing a system's inhabited worlds. They savage troop landings but are outranged by heavy warships.

buildings.name: Dilithium Refinery
buildings.description: Raw dilithium ore is useless to a warp core until it is refined and recrystallized. This plant does that work, and starship construction depends on it.

buildings.name: Phoenix Facility
buildings.description: An intelligence archive that records everything each operative learns in real time. When an agent falls, the mission does not fall with them.

buildings.name: Aquaculture Center
buildings.description: Floating sea farms that turn an ocean world's shallows into cultivated fishing grounds. Raises food output.

buildings.name: Private Farms
buildings.description: State support for family-run farms that trade some efficiency for pride and quality. Adds food and raises morale.

buildings.name: Theoretical Simulators
buildings.description: Computing halls where theorists test ideas against virtual universes before running a single real experiment. Raises the system's research output.

buildings.name: Subatomic Simulators
buildings.description: Particle laboratories fed by a dedicated warp reactor, able to recreate conditions found only inside stars. A large boost to the system's research output.

buildings.name: Subspace Scanner
buildings.description: A ground-based array that listens for the ripple a warp drive leaves in subspace. Extends sensor range.

buildings.name: Listening Post
buildings.description: A remote station whose analysts can pick a single warp signature out of a sector's background noise. Sees farther than a basic scanner.

buildings.name: Isolinear Scanner
buildings.description: Isolinear processing lets this array sift faint warp traces from much deeper space. Long sensor range without giving its position away.

buildings.name: Basic Shipyard
buildings.description: Orbital docks and construction slips where starships are assembled, overhauled and resupplied. Required to build ships, and a source of fleet supply.

buildings.name: Forced-labor Farms
buildings.description: Convict gangs work the fields under guard. The harvest improves; the public mood does not.

buildings.name: Trade Center
buildings.description: A bustling commodities exchange that draws merchants from neighboring systems. Raises the system's credit income.

buildings.name: Trade Goods
buildings.description: Instead of building projects, the system's factories turn out goods for market. Converts industry into credits.

buildings.name: Wind Turbines
buildings.description: Towering rotor farms planted where nothing else will grow, spinning in near-constant gales. Raises the system's energy output.

buildings.name: Shield Generator
buildings.description: Starship deflector technology scaled up to cover whole cities. It is not impenetrable, but it turns a massacre from orbit into a siege.

buildings.name: Union Shipyard
buildings.description: Cardassian construction slips run with military discipline. Builds and repairs the Union's ships and extends its fleet supply.

buildings.name: Re-education Center
buildings.description: Compulsory classes in loyalty for anyone who complains too loudly. Suppresses unrest, whatever its graduates privately think.

buildings.name: Obsidian Order
buildings.description: Cardassia's secret police, whose files hold something on everyone. Strengthens internal security; few citizens care to test it.

buildings.name: Covert Sensor Array
buildings.description: A military sensor net hidden inside what looks like harmless civilian astronomy. Long sensor range that enemies rarely think to target.

buildings.name: Central Command
buildings.description: The high command of the Cardassian military, and the school every officer must pass. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Labor Camp
buildings.description: Guarded work compounds where the unemployed and the unwanted are made productive. Industry rises, at a cost in morale.

buildings.name: Inquisition
buildings.description: Door-to-door interrogations until someone names the ringleaders. Restores order to a troubled system.

buildings.name: Fantasy Land
buildings.description: A Ferengi holiday world of holosuites, casinos and spas, every one metered by the minute. Raises morale and pulls in tourist latinum.

buildings.name: Holo Cinema
buildings.description: Public holosuites where anyone can star in their own adventure for an evening. Raises morale.

buildings.name: Commerce Authority
buildings.description: The Alliance's regulatory arm audits every business, and its auditors report on more than accounts. Improves Ferengi espionage.

buildings.name: Tower of Commerce
buildings.description: The Alliance's trade licensing bureau, which takes its cut of every cargo that moves. Raises the income of every trade route.

buildings.name: Franchise Office
buildings.description: Where the Alliance registers its trademarks and bills the galaxy for using them. Generates credits.

buildings.name: Festival of Fun
buildings.description: A mandatory shopping holiday; nothing calms a restless Ferengi world like a sale. Quells unrest.

buildings.name: Genesis Research Lab
buildings.description: A Federation institute chasing the dream of making dead worlds live. Boosts Biotech research.

buildings.name: Daystrom Institute
buildings.description: Richard Daystrom's legacy: the Federation's leading computer science center, home of the duotronic revolution. Boosts Computers research.

buildings.name: Federation Council
buildings.description: The Federation's parliament, where every member world has a seat and a voice. Raises contentment across the Federation.

buildings.name: Starfleet Academy
buildings.description: The school in San Francisco where Starfleet officers are made. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Utopia Planitia
buildings.description: The great orbital yards above Mars, birthplace of Starfleet's most famous ships. Speeds starship production.

buildings.name: Martial Law
buildings.description: Curfews, checkpoints and troops in the streets. A blunt last resort against unrest.

buildings.name: Hall of Warriors
buildings.description: A great hall hung with the banners of legendary warriors, where young Klingons swear to earn a place among them. Strengthens ground combat.

buildings.name: Mining Prison
buildings.description: A frozen penal colony where convicts dig dilithium until their sentences, or they, run out. Produces dilithium, and resentment with it.

buildings.name: Great Hall
buildings.description: Seat of the High Council on Qo'noS, where the Great Houses feud, bargain and swear loyalty. Raises contentment across the Empire.

buildings.name: Tactical College
buildings.description: Where Klingon officers study the battles of their ancestors, and of their enemies. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Police State
buildings.description: The Council suspends custom and lets its enforcers settle matters personally. Quells unrest.

buildings.name: Combat Testing Center
buildings.description: A weapons range where new disruptors and torpedoes are fired until they break or prove themselves. Boosts Weapons research.

buildings.name: Singularity Plant
buildings.description: Romulan engineers bottle artificial black holes to power their warp cores. It frees the fleet from dilithium and works on any world.

buildings.name: Astrophysics Academy
buildings.description: Romulan astronomers catalogue every star and anomaly within reach, and some beyond it. Boosts Energy research.

buildings.name: Imperial Senate
buildings.description: The Senate chamber on Romulus, where the Empire's nobles debate and plot. Raises contentment across the Empire.

buildings.name: TalShiar Headquarters
buildings.description: The Empire's feared intelligence service, answerable to almost no one. Strengthens internal security.

buildings.name: Naval Academy
buildings.description: Romulan officer training, heavy on patience, deception and the cloak. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Tribunal
buildings.description: Swift closed-door trials for anyone suspected of disloyalty. Quells unrest.

buildings.name: Alliance Shipyard
buildings.description: Ferengi docks where every bolt is invoiced. Builds and repairs Alliance ships and extends fleet supply.

buildings.name: Federation Replicator
buildings.description: Starfleet-standard food synthesizers installed across a colony's public spaces. Raises the system's food output by a percentage.

buildings.name: Starfleet Shipyard
buildings.description: A Starfleet yard where ships are built, refitted and sent back out. Required for construction and a source of fleet supply.

buildings.name: Military Shipyard
buildings.description: Klingon war docks where new ships are forged and battle damage is mended. Required for construction and a source of fleet supply.

buildings.name: Acamarian Clan Hall
buildings.description: Neutral ground where Acamarian clans settle disputes with words instead of blood. Raises credits and morale; requires Acamarian residents.

buildings.name: Andorian War College
buildings.description: Andorian officers teach the hard-won art of close combat. New ships gain experience; requires Andorian residents.

buildings.name: Super Soldier Academy
buildings.description: Angosian veterans pass on the conditioning that made them the most dangerous soldiers of their war. Strengthens ground combat; requires Angosian residents.

buildings.name: Mustering Base
buildings.description: An Antican recruiting depot that never lacks volunteers while the Selay live. Strengthens ground defense; requires Antican residents.

buildings.name: Harvesting Complex
buildings.description: Deep-water trawlers and processing ships working the Antedean seas. Raises food output; requires Antedean residents.

buildings.name: Bajoran Jalanda Forum
buildings.description: A public amphitheater where vedeks and citizens debate the issues of the day. Guards against unrest; requires Bajoran residents.

buildings.name: Architectural Center
buildings.description: Bandi designers, famous for their hospitality architecture, share their craft with the empire. Boosts Construction research; requires Bandi residents.

buildings.name: Industrial Center
buildings.description: Benzite process engineers publish a new procedure manual every week, and are usually right. Raises the system's industry; requires Benzite residents.

buildings.name: Counseling Academy
buildings.description: Betazoid telepaths train counselors who can feel resentment long before it turns to sabotage. Strengthens internal security; requires Betazoid residents.

buildings.name: Cosmetology Center
buildings.description: Bolian beauty clinics with a discreet back room, where agents leave looking like someone else entirely. Improves espionage success; requires Bolian residents.

buildings.name: Planetary Computer
buildings.description: The central computer every Bynar pair is linked to, now working the empire's research problems alongside its own. Boosts Computers research; requires Bynar residents.

buildings.name: Research Think Tank
buildings.description: A Caldonian institute where scholars pursue questions for their own sake, and find useful answers anyway. Raises empire research; requires Caldonian residents.

buildings.name: Gladiatorial Arena
buildings.description: Chalnoth fight here with the newest weapons, and the survivors report which ones worked. Boosts Weapons research; requires Chalnoth residents.

buildings.name: Palace of Edo
buildings.description: Gardens, games and festivities open to every visitor who keeps the rules. Raises morale; requires Edo residents.

buildings.name: Ktarian Game Studio
buildings.description: Designers of entertainment so compelling that enemy crews stop working to play it. Improves sabotage; requires Ktarian residents.

buildings.name: Kinetics Laboratory
buildings.description: Malcorian warp-field theorists, freed from secrecy, test radical engine concepts. Boosts Propulsion research; requires Malcorian residents.

buildings.name: Mintakan Farm
buildings.description: Terraced village farms tended with patient Mintakan care. Raises food output; requires Mintakan residents.

buildings.name: Monument of Surrender
buildings.description: A quiet memorial listing every conqueror the Mizarians have outlived. Steadies morale; requires Mizarian residents.

buildings.name: Recruitment Center
buildings.description: A Nausicaan hiring hall where mercenaries sign on for garrison duty across the empire. Strengthens ground combat; requires Nausicaan residents.

buildings.name: Collection Facility
buildings.description: A Pakled warehouse of salvaged, traded and borrowed technology, some of which actually works. Raises research; requires Pakled residents.

buildings.name: Selay Mustering Base
buildings.description: A Selay recruiting depot that never lacks volunteers while the Anticans live. Strengthens ground defense; requires Selay residents.

buildings.name: Bioengineering Center
buildings.description: Sheliak laboratories that reshape living systems with legal precision. Boosts Biotech research; requires Sheliak residents.

buildings.name: Physics Institute
buildings.description: Takaran physicists study the forces that act on matter, a subject close to their own unusual biology. Boosts Energy research; requires Takaran residents.

buildings.name: Defense Network
buildings.description: Layered Talarian bunkers, minefields and gun pits built to make any landing a slaughter. Greatly strengthens ground defense; requires Talarian residents.

buildings.name: Mythology Library
buildings.description: The Tamarian store of legends, read at last as the technical record it partly is. A large research boost; requires Tamarian residents.

buildings.name: Research Committee
buildings.description: A Trill council that reviews research with the memory of many past lifetimes. Raises empire research; requires Trill residents.

buildings.name: Psychohistorical Archive
buildings.description: Ullian telepathic interviews, catalogued as a map of how other peoples think. Aids intelligence work; requires Ullian residents.

buildings.name: Science Academy
buildings.description: Vulcan's ancient center of learning, where every hypothesis must survive logic. Raises empire research; requires Vulcan residents.

buildings.name: Intelligence Service
buildings.description: Yridian data dealers who now sell mostly to one customer: the empire. Improves espionage and security; requires Yridian residents.

buildings.name: Military Academy
buildings.description: Zakdorn war-gamers run crews through simulated campaigns until nothing surprises them. New ships enter service with considerable experience; requires Zakdorn residents.

buildings.name: Organic Regenerators
buildings.description: Closed-loop recyclers that return crop residue and spoiled stock to the food chain. Raises food output.

buildings.name: Imperial Shipyard
buildings.description: Romulan construction yards hidden behind layers of sensor screens. Required for construction and a source of fleet supply.
